FDA to Require Stronger Warning Labels on OTC Painkillers

As if people don't have enough to worry about. Now the otc painkillers people use to counter the headaches some suffer as a side effect of their anti-depressants might be increasing their risk of brain hemorrhage. OUCH!

Don't be worried, this may be a sensationalist new. In the adult, there are mainly two types of intracranial hemorrhage: subarachnoid hemorrhage and intracerebral hemorrhage. Subarachnoid hemorrhage occurs when an aneurysm -an abnormal outpouching of an artery in the brain- ruptures. So if you don't have an aneurysm, you most likely won't have a subarachnoid hemorrhage. As for intracerebral hemorrhage, the main and strongest risk factor is uncontrolled hypertension. Here, the pressure on the terminal, thinnest arteries in the brain is so high that they break and start bleeding. But if you don't have hypertension, you are mostly safe.

I found the original article here. I don't have time to read it right now, but I skimmed through it and it states a 1.6 hazard ratio for intracranial hemorrhage for those taking both antidepressants and NSAIDs against those only taking antidepressants. I don't know if they adjusted for any other comorbidities.

However, NSAIDs have already too much adverse effects. I mean, I would worry much more about the renal disease the chronic NSAIDs intake causes, or about the gastrointestinal ulcers and bleedings they may cause. Those are already proven risks. The risk of intracranial hemorrhage is just a new finding, which I'll read later in more depth.
